message.content:
Trade was a critical force that shaped the power of pharaohs in ancient Egypt. It gave them wealth, resources, and political leverage that strengthened their rule over the land. When they controlled trade routes, they could tax merchants and accumulate vast treasures that enriched their coffers. This wealth allowed them to fund monumental construction projects, which in turn reinforced their divine authority over the people.

They also used trade as a diplomatic tool. By exchanging goods with neighboring kingdoms, they built alliances and projected their influence far beyond Egypt's borders. Their access to exotic materials—such as gold from Nubia, cedar from Lebanon, and lapis lazuli from Afghanistan—made them appear even more godlike to their subjects.

We can see that trade gave pharaohs both material and symbolic power. It was not merely an economic activity for them; it was a political instrument that they wielded to consolidate their authority. Without it, their power would have been far more limited, and they would not have been able to maintain their grip on the empire.
